issues.description: Test changes use a zero-amount addition to bytes32.zeros — invariant of the test is silently changed
issues.detail: The tests previously passed `additions=[]` to exercise the legacy single-output path; now they pass a single zero-amount addition to the zero puzzle hash. The loop invariant of `cat_spend` ("exactly one of additions/(amount,inner_address) is meaningful") is no longer being tested on the legacy branch. State which code path each test is exercising, or split into two tests.

issues.description: `cat_discrepancy_validation` uses `None in {...}` set membership — correct but the invariant is unstated
issues.detail: The function relies on the fact that `None in {a,b,c}` returns True iff any is None, after the all-None case is handled. This is subtle (set membership on a heterogeneous set including Program-bearing strings) and deserves an inline comment naming the invariant: "on entry, at least one of the three is non-None; this branch fires iff not all three are non-None." Without the comment the reader must reconstruct the case analysis.

issues.description: `Addition` constructed by positional args without field-name discipline
issues.detail: Both new call sites build `Addition(request.amount, decode_puzzle_hash(...), request.memos)` positionally. `Addition` is a Streamable dataclass whose field order is part of an over-the-wire contract; reordering fields silently miscompiles callers. Use keyword arguments (`amount=...`, `puzzle_hash=...`, `memos=...`) so the call survives field reorderings and reads literately at the call site.

issues.description: `CreateSignedTransaction` now carries CAT-only fields without stating the validity invariant
issues.detail: Three CAT-specific fields (`extra_delta`, `tail_reveal`, `tail_solution`) plus `puzzle_decorator` are appended with a brief comment but no `__post_init__` check that they are only present when meaningful (e.g., CAT wallet, or all-or-none for the discrepancy triple at construction time, not just when the property is read). The invariant "these three are all-None or all-set" should be enforced at construction, not deferred to the property accessor.

issues.description: Comment "opportunity to raise" is cryptic; the discarded return deserves a literate note
issues.detail: Both refactored handlers call `get_wallet(...)` purely for its side effect of raising on wrong type, discarding the returned wallet, with only the comment `# opportunity to raise`. A literate one-liner — "Validate wallet exists and is of the required type; the wallet object itself is unused because create_signed_transaction re-resolves it" — would save the next reader a grep.

issues.description: Duplicated `cat_discrepancy` property on two request types — DRY but coupling is hidden
issues.detail: `CATSpend.cat_discrepancy` and `CreateSignedTransaction.cat_discrepancy` now share `cat_discrepancy_validation` but the two request types are otherwise independent. A reader has to discover that both forward to the same helper, and any future divergence (e.g., CATSpend tightening validation) will silently apply to CreateSignedTransaction. A short docstring on the helper naming both call sites would close the loop.

review.summary: Verdict: UNDER-AUDITED with NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT in several spots. The refactor is sound in spirit — consolidating three endpoints onto one signed-transaction path reduces duplication — but the invariants that make it correct are not written down. The extracted `cat_discrepancy_validation` relies on a subtle `None in {set}` idiom that should be commented; `CreateSignedTransaction` gains CAT-only fields without a `__post_init__` enforcing the all-or-none triple at construction; and `Addition` is constructed positionally at the new call sites, which couples correctness to field order in a Streamable type. Test changes from `additions=[]` to a zero-amount addition silently change which code path is being exercised and deserve a comment or a split. None of this is asymptotically wrong; it is the kind of code-as-literature work that turns a working refactor into one the next reader can trust.
